notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 08/30/2025
Patient: Joannie Kiehn, 73-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 08/30/2025. The study assessed sleep stages and respiratory events throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 37.5 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 13% of all events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent desaturations associated with apneas, with a minimum saturation of 82%. Sleep architecture was preserved with normal cycling through REM and non-REM stages. These findings indicate severe sleep-disordered breathing with a notable component of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and treatment planning are advised.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/20/2026
Patient: Joannie Kiehn, 74-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ms. Kiehn has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. She reports consistent nightly use of the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 28.4 kg/m2.

Assessment:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 24.7 events/hour on CPAP at 10 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options given CPAP failure.
2. Evaluate for possible adjustment of pressure settings or alternative devices.
3. Schedule follow-up sleep study to reassess apnea severity and treatment efficacy.
4. Continue monitoring adherence and symptoms closely.

Summary:
Ms. Kiehn demonstrates persistent obstructive sleep apnea despite adherence to CPAP therapy at current settings. Further evaluation and management adjustments are warranted to improve control of her sleep-disordered breathing.
